entity.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
entity.description: The only U.S. president elected four times, who led from a wheelchair. Overcame paralysis to defeat the Great Depression with the New Deal, guided America through World War II, and died in office weeks before victory in Europe. Historians consistently rank him among the three greatest presidents.

story.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
story.description: Paralyzed at 39, elected president at 50, launches the New Deal, leads the Allies through WWII, and dies in office 18 days before Hitler's suicide. Four terms that remade America.

moments.name: Franklin Roosevelt Is Born into American Aristocracy at Hyde Park
moments.subtitle: A privileged childhood on a Hudson Valley estate that will become a presidential landmark
moments.description: On January 30, 1882, Franklin Delano Roosevelt was born at Springwood, his family's estate in Hyde Park, New York. His father James was a wealthy businessman and Bourbon Democrat; his mother Sara Ann Delano would dominate his early life. The Roosevelts were one of America's most prominent families. As a child, James once took Franklin to meet President Grover Cleveland, who reportedly said to the boy, 'I am making a strange wish for you. It is that you may never be President of the United States.' Franklin would go on to win the presidency four times, more than any other person in American history.

moments.name: Roosevelt Is Paralyzed at 39 and Told He Will Never Walk Again
moments.subtitle: An illness on a Canadian island nearly ends a political career that has barely begun
moments.description: In August 1921, while vacationing at the family's summer home on Campobello Island, New Brunswick, Canada, Franklin Roosevelt fell ill with a paralytic disease that permanently robbed him of the use of his legs. He was 39 years old and had already served as a New York state senator and assistant secretary of the Navy. Doctors told him he would never walk unaided again. Rather than retiring from public life, Roosevelt spent years in grueling rehabilitation and developed techniques to appear mobile in public, using leg braces and leaning on aides. His wife Eleanor's encouragement helped him return to politics, winning the governorship of New York in 1928.

moments.name: Roosevelt Launches the New Deal in His First 100 Days as President
moments.subtitle: A landslide winner tells a nation in crisis that the only thing to fear is fear itself
moments.description: On March 4, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt was inaugurated as the 32nd president of the United States in Washington, D.C., after defeating Herbert Hoover in a landslide. With unemployment at 25% and thousands of banks failing, Roosevelt told Americans that 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.' In his first 100 days, he spearheaded unprecedented federal legislation: the Emergency Banking Act, the Civilian Conservation Corps, the Agricultural Adjustment Act, and the Tennessee Valley Authority. These programs formed the core of the New Deal, which fundamentally transformed the relationship between Americans and their federal government.

moments.name: Roosevelt Asks Congress for War After Japan Attacks Pearl Harbor
moments.subtitle: A president who promised to keep America out of war now asks Congress to enter it
moments.description: On December 8, 1941, one day after Japan's surprise attack on Pearl Harbor killed over 2,400 Americans, President Franklin Roosevelt addressed a joint session of Congress in Washington, D.C. He called December 7 'a date which will live in infamy' and requested a declaration of war against Japan. Congress approved within 33 minutes, with only one dissenting vote. Within days, Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy declared war on the United States, and Roosevelt obtained declarations against them too. The speech committed the world's largest industrial economy to total war and ultimately tipped the balance of World War II toward the Allies.

moments.name: Roosevelt Dies in Office Weeks Before Victory in Europe
moments.subtitle: The president who led America through its greatest war never sees it end
moments.description: On April 12, 1945, President Franklin D. Roosevelt died of a cerebral hemorrhage at the Little White House in Warm Springs, Georgia. He was 63 years old and had been president for over 12 years, serving an unprecedented four terms. He had been sitting for a portrait when he complained of a terrible headache and lost consciousness. He died that afternoon. Germany surrendered 26 days later. Roosevelt had guided the nation through the Great Depression and nearly all of World War II, but never saw the final victory. His death elevated Vice President Harry Truman, who would make the decision to use the atomic bomb.
moments.address: Little White House, Warm Springs, Georgia
